en.title: Stardew Valley's Magic: The Gathering Art Sparks Fan Uproar
en.summary: A new Magic: The Gathering Secret Lair drop brings the beloved world of Stardew Valley to the trading card game. However, the artwork for some iconic characters has left dedicated fans feeling more than a little disappointed.
en.body:
The charming and deceptively deep world of **Stardew Valley** is making a surprising leap into the **Magic: The Gathering** multiverse with a special Secret Lair drop. These limited-edition releases are known for their unique themes, often bringing beloved franchises like **Monty Python**, **Dwarf Fortress**, and even **Garfield** into **Magic**'s iconic gameplay. Now, it's the turn of **ConcernedApe**'s farm-life sim to get the **Magic** treatment, with cards inspired by the game's daily activities and characters set to arrive in July 2026.

However, the initial reveal of the **Stardew Valley** Secret Lair has ignited a passionate debate within the game's dedicated community. The core of the controversy lies in the artistic interpretation of certain characters, particularly the romantic bachelor **Elliott**. While fans have long envisioned him as a willowy, bishonen-esque figure, the artwork for the **Mermaid's Pendant** card, a reskin of **Magic**'s **Wedding Ring** card, presents a much more traditionally masculine, square-jawed interpretation. This stark contrast has not sat well with many.

## Fan Reaction and Visual Disconnect

The **Stardew Valley** subreddit has become a hotbed of discussion and, frankly, roasting. Players have unleashed a torrent of creative criticism, comparing the depicted **Elliott** to characters from **Habbo Hotel**, **Sheriff Woody**, and even members of the famously inbred **House of Habsburg**. The sentiment of "We have **Elliot** at home" has become a common refrain, with some fans even joking about switching their romantic affections to other characters like **Alex**. Similar critiques have been leveled at other cards, with **Penny**'s depiction reportedly deviating from her established in-game appearance, trading her signature buns for ringlets.

## What's Next

This **Stardew Valley** x **Magic: The Gathering** Secret Lair drop is slated for release in July 2026. While the full scope of the collection and the specific mechanics of the cards are still being revealed, the community's strong reaction underscores the deep emotional connection players have with **Stardew Valley**'s characters and their own interpretations of its world. It remains to be seen if future reveals will appease the fanbase or if this artistic divergence will become a lasting talking point for the crossover.

content_raw: The limited releases of cards for Magic: The Gathering that are mostly reskins of existing cards with new art are called Secret Lair drops. They're infamous for selling out fast and being hard to get hold of at normal prices, and they're also infamous for having unusual themes. There's been a Monty Python one , a Dwarf Fortress one , and even a Garfield one . Next? Stardew Valley. ConcernedApe's quirky farm-life sim has a legion of dedicated fans who have built their own mimetic lore on top of the actual story of the game, like Overwatch stans interpreting and shipping characters in ways Blizzard didn't intend. Take Elliott, for instance, a sentimental writer who lives on the beach and is among Stardew Valley's romanceable cast. According to fan artists, he's a willowy bishonen boy. According to ConcernedApe's own art for the Mermaid's Pendant card, a reskin of the existing Wedding Ring card, he's a square-jawed Chad. They've called him a "Habbo hotel looking mf" and roasted his "Sheriff Woody lookin’ ass". He's been compared to Matt Smith's character in House of the Dragon, Fabio, and a member of the famously inbred House of Hapsburg, while others declare "We have Elliot at home" and say "I might have to marry Alex now." Other cards show Penny with ringlets rather than the buns players assumed she had based on the in-game art, and depict Leah as substantially thicker than you might have assumed she would be. To be fair, most players aren't complaining about the latter, or the glow-up Clint has received just in time to become a marriage candidate in the 1.7 update. Personally, I like the way these cards look. Sword to Plowshares is a perfect Magic card to be given a Stardew makeover, and little details like the autopetter you can see inside the cave chest speak to a real affection for the, well, I guess it's the deep lore of Stardew Valley. There's even a card for the mayor's purple underpants. ConcernedApe's illustrations in particular have always been a bit on the "programmer art" end of the spectrum, from the moment you see grandpa's odd-looking bed at the start of the game. These are exactly the kind of human imperfections that give art personality, and make Stardew Valley distinctive among all the copycats. But I thought Elliott's jaw seemed pretty robust even when seen in profile, so what do I know. The Stardew Valley Magic cards will be on sale from 9 am on July 27 at the Secret Lair website .
